name: shiftmap-min-max-reduce-an-eight-by-eight-blur-map
rationale:
Covers air.atomic.local.min.s.i32 and air.atomic.local.max.s.i32, the two threadgroup atomics with the most case-less corpus sources, together with the pixel-coordinate air.gather_texture_2d.v4f16 that feeds them. The kernel's static addrspace(3) [2 x atomic i32] is seeded to INT_MAX/INT_MIN by thread (0,0), reduced into by every thread, and read back after the second barrier, so a lost or mis-ordered atomic changes the answer.

Loop bound: both loops step the thread's texel origin by a whole grid, x by (gid.x+32)*4 and y by (gid.y+16)*4, and exit once that origin leaves the texture. On an 8x8 input the next origin is 128 and 64 texels out, so every thread runs exactly one iteration of each loop and the kernel is straight-line in practice.

Grid (2,2,1) in one threadgroup of (2,2,1) puts all four threads on the same two atomic slots and tiles the 8x8 input with four disjoint 4x4 blocks. Each thread gathers at its origin plus (1,1), (1,3), (3,1) and (3,3); the embedded sampler is coord::pixel with filter::nearest and clamp_to_edge, so the four bilinear footprints are the texel pairs {0,1} and {2,3} on each axis and together they are exactly the thread's 4x4 block. The extremes sit at the two far corners, 0.25 at texel (0,0) and 0.75 at texel (7,7): a footprint that is shifted, clamped or short of four gathers loses one of them and moves the result.

Exactness: every input texel is a multiple of 2^-5 in [0.25, 0.75], so multiplying by 65536 is an integer and the fast_floor and fast_ceil that follow are no-ops whatever variant runs them; the products stay under 49152, far inside i32. The reduction therefore yields min 16384 and max 49152, scaled back by 2^-16 to exactly 0.25 and 0.75. Their difference is 0.5, so the final fdiv is 1/0.5 = 2 and is exact under fast:: and precise:: alike. Expected texel (0,0) of the rgba32_float output is (0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 2.0).

name: add-signed-bytes-into-unsigned-bytes-and-clamp
rationale: Metal ground truth for the four uncovered AIR symbols this kernel is made of: air.convert.s.v3i32.s.v3i8, air.convert.s.v3i32.u.v3i8, air.clamp.s.v3i32 and air.convert.u.v3i8.s.v3i32 (5 case-less sources). The kernel sign-extends a packed_char3 from buffer 0, zero-extends the packed_uchar3 already in buffer 1, adds them, clamps to [0, 255] and truncates back to three bytes, so every step is integer and the result is exact regardless of fast-math reassociation. Four texels pin both extensions and both clamp ends: texel 0 is char3(-100, -128, 127) over uchar3(200, 0, 255), whose x is 100 only if the signed source really sign-extends (zero-extending 0x9C gives 356, which clamps to 255) and the unsigned destination really zero-extends (sign-extending 0xC8 gives -56, so the sum would clamp to 0); its y saturates at the low end and its z at the high end. Texel 1 lands exactly on 255 without clamping and pins a -1 that would read 255 unsigned, texel 2 clamps only its y, and texel 3 stays inside the range untouched. The uint2 in buffer 2 is the (4, 1) grid extent the kernel bounds-checks against, so all four threads store.

name: four-multisample-reads-at-two-samples
rationale: Metal ground truth for six uncovered multisample read families: air.read_texture_2d_ms.u.v4i16 (3 case-less corpus sources), air.read_texture_2d_ms.u.v4i32 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.s.v4i32 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.i16.v4f16 (2), air.read_texture_2d_ms.i16.u.v4i16 (2) and air.read_depth_2d_ms.f32 (2) -- 13 sources. A multisample read takes one operand an ordinary read does not, the sample index, and it is the operand a lowering can silently drop because every sample of a texel is a plausible answer for that texel. The four threads therefore read four different texels at two different samples, and every stored value encodes its own (x, y, sample) triple, so a read that ignored the sample index or took it from the coordinate lands a value the derivation places somewhere else. The two u.v4i16 symbols differ only in operand width -- .i16. is a ushort2 coordinate and ushort sample, the other uint2 and uint -- and they read the same texture through different channels, so a lowering that widened one wrongly disagrees with the other where both must be right. Every value is an integer well inside its type or an exact binary fraction.

name: constant-half4-zero

name: cube-texel-read-beside-a-cube-sample
rationale: A cube texel read on a cube the same kernel also direction-samples. SPIR-V has no cube texel fetch -- OpImageFetch forbids Dim Cube -- so read() is lowered as a sample along a direction aimed at the exact centre of the named texel, through a sampler the translator invents because no Metal argument supplies one. That descriptor is reported as SynthesizedReadSampler, and the executor had no arm for the kind at all: no consumer could build a pipeline for a module containing one, so this family had no case and could not have had one. The state the sampler must be bound with -- nearest at magnification, minification and between mip levels -- was recorded only in a comment in the lowering. The cube stays Dim Cube because it is sampled as well as read; a cube only read is declared as something SPIR-V can fetch and no sampler is invented. Faces 0-3 carry a distinct value per texel, so the four reads on them measure the face index, the in-face coordinate, and the direction the translator builds to reach that texel: 1, 12, 23, 34. Faces 4 and 5 are uniform, 41 and 54, and are what the two samples aim at along the exact +Z and -Z axes -- a sample at the centre of a uniform face is the same value under any filter or address mode, so those lanes measure the sampling path and nothing about cube corner conventions. Every value is a small integer, exact in binary32.

name: compact-live-depth-bins-by-a-two-level-lane-prefix-sum
rationale: A 32x32 threadgroup is 32 SIMD groups of 32 lanes, and thread_index_in_threadgroup is y*32 + x, so SIMD group s is exactly image row s. Each lane flags its texel with air.convert.u.i1.f.f16 (zero) or the shader's own NaN bit test, air.simd_sum.u.i16 counts the flags per row, one air.simd_prefix_inclusive_sum.u.i16 turns those 32 row counts into row bases, and a second one gives each lane its rank inside its row. The compaction then writes every live texel index at its rank, which is what makes both prefix sums observable: a wrong base or a wrong within-row rank moves entries rather than changing their values. 329 of the 1024 texels are flagged -- some +0.0, some -0.0 and some quiet NaN, so a > 0 test or a bit-equality test against positive zero would both disagree -- and the surviving 695 indices land in ascending order over the first 1390 bytes, with the tail of the buffer left at its poisoned initial value. Every value is an exact ushort, so nothing here has rounding or association freedom.

name: one-output-pixel-four-channel-fma-accumulation
rationale:
First coverage of air.fma.f16, whose 108 case-less corpus sources are the largest uncovered count reachable by an exact byte comparison. The AIR is an Espresso v9 half-accumulating convolution; the function constants collapse it to its smallest live shape -- one 1x1 kernel tap, one convolution group, unit strides, no upsampling, no k-splitting -- so a single invocation at gid (0,0,0) computes one output pixel of four channels from four input channels. That is exactly sixteen chained air.fma.f16 calls, four per output channel, plus the bias add. F_activation is 3, which is the switch's default arm and applies no activation, so the module's five air.tanh.f16 calls stay out of the executed region: half tanh is one of the intrinsics whose fast:: and precise:: Metal variants disagree, and an exact comparison could not survive it.

Every authored value is a small integer, which is what makes the comparison exact rather than approximate. src is [1,2,3,4]; the four weight rows are [1,2,3,4], [5,6,7,8], [-1,3,-5,7] and [10,20,30,40], giving channel sums 30, 70, 18 and 300; the biases are [1000,-1000,7,0.5], so the answer is [1030,-930,25,300.5]. Every individual product and every running partial sum -- 1, 5, 14, 30 / 5, 17, 38, 70 / -1, 5, -10, 18 / 10, 50, 140, 300 -- is an exactly representable binary16 value, and so is each final sum (binary16 holds every integer to 2048, and 300.5 sits on a quarter-ulp grid). The result therefore does not depend on the order the four products are accumulated or on whether fast math reassociates the dependent fma chain, so a mismatch here is a lowering difference and not a rounding one.

The output buffer starts as eight poison bytes, so a kernel that returned through any of the four early exits at %34, %41, %46 or %378 without storing would be visible rather than silently passing. The distinct weight rows make each of the four accumulators independent: reading one output channel's weights for another would return 30 where -930 is written.

execution_safety is authored_bounded. All three loops are bounded by authored values: the kernel loops run F_kernel_size_y = 1 and F_kernel_size_x = 1 times, and the channel-block loop compares against end_k_split - start_k_split, which the params set to one block.
